page: Microsoft Azure E64as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7763 processor configured with 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs running at 3.525 GHz. Memory capacity totals 512.0 GB, providing an 8.0 GB allocation per vCPU. Storage configuration includes a 928 GB local SSD alongside support for Premium Storage volumes. Dedicated hardware accelerators are not included, with a GPU count of zero.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel compute and high memory responsiveness. PassMark memory testing places the system in the top 10% tier. Multi-threaded performance is similarly competitive, reflected in top 25% results across stress-ng multi-core tests, PassMark CPU evaluation (62243.41), and Geekbench multi-core runs (17837.0). Single-threaded tasks, such as Geekbench single-core execution (1614.0) and single-threaded gzip compression (25.88 GB/sec), register within the middle 50% band. Large block uncached memory bandwidth reaches 107.94 GB/sec for reads and 51.36 GB/sec for writes.

The dense 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio renders the system effective for memory-bound applications, including in-memory datastores and relational databases. This is supported by 62.62 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and upper-quartile PassMark database scores. However, the platform lacks AVX-512 vector support and discrete GPUs, causing large model AI execution to degrade, as indicated by 70B parameter LLM generation falling into the bottom 25% bracket. Primary workload fits include high-memory databases, Redis caching layers, ETL pipelines, and multi-threaded compilation.
